L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo con 332 titoli in ribasso rispetto a 167 in rialzo, mentre il Nasdaq-100 ha sottoperformato con un calo medio più marcato del negativo 1,04 percento rispetto al negativo 0,68 percento dell'S&P 500. Il Dow Jones, nel frattempo, ha registrato 23 ribassi rispetto a soli 7 rialzi, con una media del negativo 0,58 percento. Nel mercato più ampio, 345 titoli sono scesi rispetto a 169 in rialzo, con un calo medio dello 0,73 percento.

I Communication Services hanno rappresentato il settore con le migliori prestazioni della seduta, in rialzo dell'1,22 percento in media, mentre i Consumer Staples si sono mantenuti relativamente stabili al negativo 0,09 percento. I titoli tecnologici hanno subito il peso maggiore del selloff, scendendo del 3,15 percento in media, seguiti da Information Technology al negativo 1,27 percento e Materials al negativo 1,06 percento. U.S. equities declined on September 10, 2026, as Treasury yields climbed toward multiyear highs and oil prices surged past $100 per barrel, stoking inflation concerns. According to the Wall Street Journal, the 10-year Treasury yield neared 5 percent amid the broader selloff, while oil futures jumped on Middle East escalation raising supply worries. The S&P 500 fell with 332 stocks declining against 167 advancing, while the Nasdaq-100 underperformed with a steeper average decline of negative 1.04 percent versus the S&P 500's negative 0.68 percent. The Dow Jones, meanwhile, saw 23 declines against only 7 advances, averaging negative 0.58 percent. Across the broader market, 345 stocks fell against 169 gainers, with an average decline of 0.73 percent.

Communication Services emerged as the session's best-performing sector, rising 1.22 percent on average, while Consumer Staples held relatively steady at negative 0.09 percent. Technology stocks bore the brunt of the selloff, declining 3.15 percent on average, followed by Information Technology at negative 1.27 percent and Materials at negative 1.06 percent. Among gainers, Skyworks Solutions jumped 9.79 percent and Reddit gained 6.08 percent, though tracked outlets reported no specific catalysts for those moves. Charter Communications rose 4.98 percent after Barron's reported the stock bouncing back following a broadband warning-driven selloff. Elevance Health advanced 4.95 percent without reported company news. Apple gained 3.56 percent, with CNBC noting the stock chart had given a classic technical signal. Ford Motor Company climbed 3.2 percent following a CNBC report of a $1 billion investment at its Kentucky plant in response to Department of Transportation criticism regarding China. AppLovin, GoDaddy, General Motors, and Take-Two Interactive also posted gains ranging from 2.76 to 3.09 percent.

On the downside, Cooper Companies posted the session's steepest loss at negative 14.67 percent, according to Barron's. Baker Hughes fell 6.66 percent, with Barron's reporting it was the stock's worst day in more than a year. Freeport-McMoRan declined 6.59 percent without reported catalyst. Hewlett Packard Enterprise dropped 6.25 percent per Financial Times. CoreWeave fell 6.13 percent and FactSet declined 5.82 percent without tracked news. Lam Research, Vertiv, Intel, and Lumentum all retreated between 5.39 and 5.65 percent. Intel's decline came as Reuters reported that Silver Lake and Intel-backed Altera were preparing an IPO that could raise over $2 billion as early as 2026.

markets_brief.prose_html: I mercati obbligazionari subiscono una pressione di vendita sostenuta a livello globale, con il rendimento decennale statunitense che si avvicina al 5% mentre i rendimenti australiani hanno raggiunto i massimi dal 2011 in mezzo a preoccupazioni legate al petrolio. Il selloff riflette dinamiche di mercato più ampie che pesano sul reddito fisso nelle economie sviluppate. Nel frattempo, i costi infrastrutturali ed energetici stanno aumentando: la rete britannica richiede un aggiornamento di 70 miliardi di sterline mentre i consumatori si preparano a bollette più alte, segnalando che le esigenze di spesa in conto capitale si stanno traducendo in pressioni sulle spese domestiche.
markets_brief.prose_html_en: Bond markets are under sustained selling pressure globally, with the U.S. 10-year yield approaching 5% while Australian yields have jumped to their highest level since 2011 amid oil-related concerns. The selloff reflects broader market dynamics weighing on fixed income across developed economies. Meanwhile, infrastructure and energy costs are mounting: the UK grid requires a £70 billion upgrade as consumers brace for higher bills, signaling that capital expenditure demands are translating into household expense pressures.
